title: Upset Sunday: All Three Unbeatens Fall and the Top of the Buckaroo Table Becomes a Four-Way Pileup
dek: Alan toppled the HULK with a running back he'd owned for one week, Zoe ran over Sonny, Kaushal finally found the win column, and now four teams share first place at 3-1.
body: Week 4 began with three undefeated teams and ended with none. No Banner only HULK, The Horse is Hea and The fumblers all walked in at 3-0 and all walked out with a loss, and three of the week's four games went to the pregame underdog. The headliner was Team Pillbert's 125.42 to 116.72 win over Ramon, a game the numbers gave Alan only a 29% chance to win at home. Javonte Williams, in his first week in Pillbert colors after arriving from Randy, scored 28.8 on a 13.25 projection, and Alan won by 8.7 despite leaving Kyle Monangai's 27.5 on his bench. Kenneth Walker III did his part for the HULK with 30.4, but Ramon's first loss of the season cost him the outright lead, and Team Pillbert's three-game winning streak has its title odds up from 9% to 21%.

The biggest single performance of the week belonged to Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN. Tetairoa McMillan exploded for 38.2 on a 13.5 projection, Bijan Robinson added 27.2, and Zoe beat Sonny 120.88 to 95.1 as a 30% home underdog. She even had cushion to spare: Nico Collins scored 27.3 from her bench. Z² is now 2-2 and has won two of her first four games as a fantasy manager, which is not how rookie seasons are supposed to go.

Sonny's afternoon was the mirror image. Parker Washington scored 1.5 on a 12.79 projection, the week's second-biggest bust, while Chuba Hubbard, the running back Sonny traded Rashee Rice to get, scored 25.4 on the bench in his first week with The Horse is Hea. The only consolation is mathematical: the margin was 25.78, so even if all 25.4 of Hubbard's points had been added with nothing taken away, Sonny still loses by 0.38. That is the kind of consolation that does not actually console anyone.

Kaushal had been waiting three weeks for something to go right, and Week 4 delivered all of it at once. Habibsters dropped 140.1, the highest score of the week, and beat The fumblers 140.1 to 96.88 despite Randy being a 61% favorite at home. CeeDee Lamb led the way with 32.8 on a 13.65 projection, and the 43.22-point margin was the week's largest. Randy got just 6 points from Stefon Diggs, the receiver he took back in the Williams deal, which made Alan's win across town sting a little extra. Kaushal's title odds jumped from 1% to 8%, and with 459.1 points he has now outscored Randy's 3-1 team despite sitting at 1-3.

The battle of the 0-3 teams went to Mekhi, whose Dawgs beat Counting or not Counting GV 107.54 to 90.22 as 63% favorites. Kyren Williams carried the load with 31.7 on an 11.88 projection, which was enough to survive Ja'Marr Chase posting 4.2 on a 16.54 projection. Jordan got the same 4.2 from Garrett Wilson on a 13.23 projection, and JMoney sits at 0-4 with a league-low 349.2 points and 0% playoff odds. To his credit, he went shopping: Kirk Cousins came in for Marvin Harrison Jr., Dalton Schultz replaced Michael Pittman Jr., and Michael Wilson took Tank Bigsby's spot.

The standings now feature a four-way tie at 3-1, sorted by points: No Banner only HULK (561), Team Pillbert (480.9), The Horse is Hea (466.7) and The fumblers (458.7). The HULK is still the clear favorite at 41% title odds and 97% playoff odds, but that is down from 52% a week ago. Behind Alan's 21%, The fumblers sit at 14% and Sonny dropped from 21% to 11%. Down the table, Zoe is 2-2 but given just 18% playoff odds, while Kaushal at 1-3 gets 38% thanks to all those points, and Mekhi sits at 22%.

The busiest man on the wire and the trade market was Alan. He pried Ashton Jeanty loose from Jordan for Isaiah Likely, Emeka Egbuka and Denzel Boston, then flipped Jeanty and Davante Adams to Mekhi for Justin Jefferson, which means Jeanty has now belonged to three teams this season. Alan also dropped De'Von Achane and Bryce Young, added Tyreek Hill, Ollie Gordon II and Kalif Raymond, and swapped kicker Jason Myers for Spencer Shrader. His discards did not last long: Ramon scooped up Myers and the Bills D/ST, and Sonny grabbed Bryce Young, along with the Bears D/ST, Tony Pollard and Juwan Johnson while cutting Mark Andrews. Elsewhere, the quarterback carousel spun hard, with Kaushal taking Sam Darnold over Drake Maye, Randy adding Trevor Lawrence and dropping Justin Herbert, and Zoe swapping Kyler Murray for Jared Goff.

Week 5 has a revenge game built right in: Dawgs host Team Pillbert, and Mekhi gets to point Jeanty and Adams at the guy who just traded them to him for Jefferson. No Banner only HULK and The fumblers meet in a battle of 3-1 teams, with Ramon trying to keep the rest of the pack at arm's length. Habibsters against The Horse is Hea is two-time champion versus reigning champion, and Kaushal's hot hand gets a real test. And Jordan faces Zoe in a matchup with household bragging rights on the line, where Ghostu-Spider SZN needs the win to climb out of .500 territory and Jordan needs it just to get on the board.

social.author: Pillbert Pep Squad
social.text: Javonte Williams: one week on the roster, 28.8 points, one dead HULK. Also we left 27.5 on the bench and STILL won. Three straight. Get used to it.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider Web Crawlers
social.text: Tetairoa McMillan was projected for 13.5. He scored 38.2. Our rookie manager is 2-2 and we are officially done being called a fluke.

social.author: Habibsters Faithful
social.text: 140.1. Top score of the week. Biggest margin of the week. CeeDee for 32.8. The two-time champ just remembered how to win and the 61% favorite found out the hard way.

social.author: Buckaroo Bench Watch
social.text: Benched points this week: Monangai 27.5, Collins 27.3, Hubbard 25.4. Two of those teams won anyway. The third traded for his guy and then sat him.

social.author: The Horse is Hea Stable Boys
social.text: Parker Washington 1.5. Hubbard 25.4 on the bench. Do the math and we still lose by 0.38, so technically nobody can blame the lineup. Technically.

social.author: Waiver Wire Wendy
social.text: Ashton Jeanty's 2026 tour: Jordan to Alan to Mekhi, all before Week 5. Somebody get that man a frequent flyer card.

social.author: Dawgs Pound Report
social.text: Kyren 31.7 on an 11.88 projection. First win of the year. And next week we get Alan, with Jeanty and Adams in our lineup. Revenge is a dish best served at flex.

social.author: Buckaroo Insider Gus
social.text: Four teams at 3-1, a 1-3 team with more points than one of them, and a 2-2 team the playoff odds barely respect. Week 4 broke the standings and nobody's fixing them.

social.author: Counting GV Booster Club
social.text: 0-4 but we added Kirk Cousins, Dalton Schultz and Michael Wilson and got three players for Jeanty. The rebuild has a pulse. A faint one.

trade_watch.take: This one went from looking lopsided on paper to lopsided on the scoreboard: Javonte Williams started and scored 28.8 in Alan's upset win, while Stefon Diggs gave Randy 6 in a 43-point loss. Week one of the deal is a 22.8-point gap, and Alan is pulling away.

The trade that dinged both teams' odds managed to give both teams zero lineup points in Week 4: Hubbard scored 25.4 on Sonny's bench and Rashee Rice put up 0 without starting for Ramon. Both sides lost, and so far nobody has actually cashed in.

bios.1: Sonny's first loss came hard, 120.88 to 95.1 against Zoe, with Parker Washington scoring 1.5 and new trade acquisition Chuba Hubbard parked on the bench. Still 3-1, but the defending champ's title odds have slid from 21% to 11%.
bios.2: Randy was a 61% favorite and lost by 43.22, scoring 96.88 while Stefon Diggs managed 6. Still 3-1 with 14% title odds, but with 458.7 points the fewest of the four first-place teams.
bios.3: Jordan is 0-4 with a league-low 349.2 points and 0% playoff odds after a loss to Mekhi. He's retooling, turning Ashton Jeanty into Isaiah Likely, Emeka Egbuka and Denzel Boston and adding Kirk Cousins, Dalton Schultz and Michael Wilson.
bios.4: Winners of three straight after knocking off the HULK as a 29% underdog, with new arrival Javonte Williams leading the way. Alan then spent the week rebuilding on the fly, ending up with Justin Jefferson and Tyreek Hill, and his title odds have climbed to 21%.
bios.5: Mekhi got off the schneid with a 107.54 to 90.22 win, carried by Kyren Williams' 31.7 while Ja'Marr Chase managed 4.2. He's 1-3, just traded Justin Jefferson for Davante Adams and Ashton Jeanty, and gets Alan, the other side of that deal, next week.
bios.6: Kaushal finally broke through with the week's top score, 140.1, and its biggest margin behind CeeDee Lamb's 32.8. The record says 1-3, but 459.1 points and a jump from 1% to 8% title odds say the two-time champ is very much alive.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut finally lost, falling 125.42 to 116.72 to Alan despite 30.4 from Kenneth Walker III. Still the league leader in points (561) and title odds (41%), but now one of four teams at 3-1 instead of the lone unbeaten.
bios.8: Zoe's rookie season keeps producing upsets, this time a 120.88 to 95.1 win over Sonny powered by Tetairoa McMillan's league-best 38.2. At 2-2 she is only given 18% playoff odds, which feels like a number she plans to argue with.
